To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the asymptotic robustness (as a function of a rare-event parameter) of estimators used in rare-event simulation can be qualified by a hierarchy of properties, (2) these properties can be characterized in terms of quantities related to Lyapunov functions, and (3) they can be used to design good estimators, in particular for rare-event simulation in the context of highly reliable Markowian systems.

the asymptotic robustness (in the sense of BRE, LE and higher-order properties) of estimators can be studied by means of Lyapunov-like conditions that can be used to guide the design of IS schemes, and that the asymptotic behavior of these properties can be studied in terms of a hierarchy of conditions that become strictly stronger with the order k.

(i) for state-dependent IS, BRM-k is equivalent to LE-k, for any k ≥ 1, (ii) for HRMS, the equivalence of the BRM-k and the LE-k properties holds for a popular class IS schemes, and (iii) the LE-k and the BRM-k properties become strictly stronger as k increases.

a general theory that provides a framework for the design and analysis of estimators in the context of importance sampling.
the study of asymptotic robustness in rare-event simulation and its implications for the design of efficient estimators.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a general theory of asymptotic robustness in rare-event simulation and have illustrated it on a number of models of interest in reliability and queueing theory.

the BRM-k and the LE-k properties are the most convenient to ensure that the variance of a statistic is under control as the rarity parameter increases, and that they are also useful to control the bias.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the asymptotic robustness behavior of estimators in simulation can be analyzed in a systematic way, by means of a hierarchy of properties, which can be used to guide the design of estimators.
, for a wide class of models, it is possible to design IS schemes with a very good asymptotic robustness profile, in the sense that all the aforementioned properties are satisfied.

, for a given model and a given estimator, the choice of the robustness properties to be used should be based on the desired level of asymptotic accuracy, and the level of robustness should be chosen accordingly.
